correctness.rationale: For all finite N and κ>0 the drift −κI+J is stable. The exact stationary Lyapunov integral yields the binomial covariance after integrating exp(−2κt) t^(2q+d)/(q!(q+d)!). Uniform de Moivre–Laplace/Stirling asymptotics when q/N≥ε and d=O(sqrt(N)) give the Gaussian spatial factor; the uniform binomial maximal-mass bound O((q+1)^−1/2) makes the omitted q<εN contribution O(sqrt(ε)). Detuning yields exp(−2ζu). Gaussian covariance convergence completes the finite-dimensional claim; integration by parts gives the erfc profile. VERIFY.py independently checked exact rational Lyapunov recursion and bounded convergence/quadrature tests (15,215 assertions). Numerical tests are not substituted for proof.

value.rationale: The theorem supplies a previously unreported full joint spatial correlation profile and finite-size detuning crossover for a naturally observed noisy one-way chain at a high-order Jordan exceptional point. This is not merely re-evaluating the known infinite-chain variance: it identifies the √N mesoscopic observation scale and N^(1/4) typical fluctuations despite fixed finite spectral gap, gives all finite-dimensional Gaussian limits and a closed erfc correlation function. The observable quantifies where near-boundary nonnormal fluctuations remain coherent and how near-critical damping alters them.
